paragraph: [Presidential Decree 267/24 of 28 November 2024 approved a plan to December 2026 for a single database fed daily by civil registration](<https://lex.ao/docs/presidente-da-republica/2024/decreto-presidencial-n-o-267-24-de-28-de-novembro/>). Births [have been registered in RCI since 2023 at civil registration posts](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099062824094544617/pdf/P179485-40c865ab-d980-432a-acf1-940f22b02d4c.pdf>). As of 2024, RCI [is in Luanda's registries and in one post each in Huambo, Benguela and Lubango](<https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/bitstreams/d1c06154-9015-4e69-9112-ccf5b7092b4a/download>). In the last twelve months, Novo Jornal reported on 5 May 2026 that [identification and civil registration posts in almost the whole country had been without their system](<https://www.novojornal.co.ao/politica/detalhe/minjusdh-diz-que-falhas-do-sistema-nos-postos-de-identificacao-e-registo-civil-que-ja-duram-ha-meses-se-devem-as-quebras-de-telecomunicacoes-71601.html>). No count of the offices registering in RCI has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

On 18 July 2026 the interior ministry's presentation [records a pilot digitalisation project in 12 communes](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-burundi_crvs_transformation_journey.pdf>). The same presentation says [the majority of civil-status acts are still recorded in physical registers](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-burundi_crvs_transformation_journey.pdf>). The project launched at Rumonge on 19 July 2024 [is for the digital registration of births and deaths at the commune's civil status service](<https://www.iwacu-burundi.org/region-sud-rumonge-enregistrement-numerique-a-letat-civil/>). In the last twelve months, on 6 May 2026 the ministry [presented a digital platform for civil registration and biometric identity card production](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/burundi-launches-digital-civil-registry-and-biometric-id-initiative>). No source has been found that says the system is past its pilot, or how the pilot record is made. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

From 20 August 2025 [the declaration and registration of a birth are done on site in about ten public health facilities](<https://www.gouv.bj/article/3209/declaration-enregistrement-obtention-acte-naissance-nouveau-jour-etat-civil-beninois-anip-lance-phase-pilote-guichet-unique-dans-plusieurs-formations-sanitaires-/>). In 2023 [174 of 233 civil-status centres in five departments were equipped for birth registration](<https://www.unicef.org/benin/recits/les-reformes-de-letat-civil-facilitent-la-d%C3%A9livrance-des-actes-de-naissance-aux-enfants>). In the last twelve months, ANIP's director general gave an account of the pilot on 16 July 2026. [The pilot ended in February 2026 and a consolidation phase is running in the same ten facilities](<https://www.lanation.bj/actualites/aristide-adjinacou-directeur-general-de-lanip-nous-voulons-faire-de-chaque-maternite-une-veritable-porte-dentree-vers-lidentite-legale>). No share of local offices registering births digitally has been found, and no plan with a period. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

The ministry reported the software [deployed in 30 main and 140 secondary centres in 2025](<https://www.wakatsera.com/strategie-nationale-de-letat-civil-2023-2027-plus-de-81-dexecution-financiere-enregistres-en-2025/>). [In 2024 it was in 20 main and 96 secondary centres](<https://www.sidwaya.info/strategie-nationale-de-letat-civil-un-taux-dexecution-physique-de-6411-en-2024/>). In the last twelve months, agents of the commune of Koloko were [trained on the software and given equipment](<https://www.aib.media/kenedougou-les-agents-de-la-mairie-de-koloko-formes-a-lutilisation-du-logiciel-veneem/>), as reported on 22 June 2026. On 25 June 2026 the director general for the modernisation of civil status said [deployment in communes was continuing](<https://www.wakatsera.com/strategie-nationale-de-letat-civil-2023-2027-plus-de-81-dexecution-financiere-enregistres-en-2025/>). No total of centres has been found, and no source says how many of the 170 register in the software. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

Statistics Botswana reported in August 2026 that the department [operates 35 district registration offices and 17 on-site registration points at hospitals and clinics](<https://statsbots.org.bw/sites/default/files/publications/Vital%20Statistics%20Report%202024.pdf>). Electronic on-site registration [had opened in 13 hospitals by September 2015](<https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/0f5b85a0-2c35-534b-bf92-0880430d4ffb/content>). In the last twelve months, the minister told Parliament on 6 March 2026 of [about 15 hospital kiosks for on-site birth registration](<https://www.parliament.gov.bw/documents/DAILY-HANSARD--6th-MARCH-2026---Budget-Meeting--2nd-meeting-of-the-2nd-session-of-the-13th-Parliament_10_05_04_11_03_2026.pdf>). [He said 9 were operating and 6 had closed](<https://www.parliament.gov.bw/documents/DAILY-HANSARD--6th-MARCH-2026---Budget-Meeting--2nd-meeting-of-the-2nd-session-of-the-13th-Parliament_10_05_04_11_03_2026.pdf>). No count of the district offices entering records in the system has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

The director general for decentralisation and civil status described [an all-paper system on 18 July 2026, with 70% of civil registration centres without electricity](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-digitisation-car.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the territorial administration ministry said in July 2026 that it [is preparing the deployment of a civil registration application with CIVIPOL as technical operator](<https://oubanguimedias.com/2026/07/20/centrafrique-le-matddl-lance-la-numerisation-des-documents-detat-civil-pour-securiser-lidentite-nationale/>). [An operational map of 45 centres had been validated](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-digitisation-car.pdf>) by 18 July 2026. No office has been found entering a birth or a death digitally, and no count of pilot offices. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

ONECI's director general said in July 2024 that [298 centres were connected to the central City Web system](<https://www.oneci.ci/actualites/1721159722>). The World Bank said on 18 September 2025 that [the registry is still on paper](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099092225092021892/pdf/BOSIB-af66fe3f-3dfc-4703-ab9c-9f1fb5cf5714.pdf>). In the last twelve months, ONECI [gave every town hall and sub-prefecture centre computers carrying the software](<https://www.aip.ci/cote-divoire-aip-loneci-renforce-les-capacites-en-logiciel-citiweb-des-agents-de-letat-civil-de-la-region-du-goh/>). On 23 October 2026 its director general said [it is deployed in all centres, with connectivity still a problem](<https://www.sikafinance.com/marches/cote-divoire-le-logiciel-national-detat-civil-deploye-la-connectivite-reste-un-defi_65266>). No share of centres registering births in the software has been found, and the 298 comes with no total. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

On 14 September 2026 BUNEC's Director General counted that [60 of 432 principal civil status centres were digitised, 13.9 per cent](<https://ecomatin.net/cameroun-52-milliards-fcfa-recherches-pour-numeriser-letat-civil>). The count was [42 in April 2022](<https://ecomatin.net/cameroun-52-milliards-fcfa-recherches-pour-numeriser-letat-civil>). On 8 October 2026 he [described paper as dominant](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202610/cameroons-civil-registration-reform-faces-85m-funding-gap>). In the last twelve months, by August 2026 [two East Region centres, Bertoua 1er and the Bertoua City Council, were in production](<https://www.undp.org/cameroon/stories/dans-lest-du-cameroun-la-digitalisation-de-letat-civil-transforme-progressivement-lacces-lidentite-legale-bertoua-cameroun-aout-2026>). No share of all local offices has been found, since the 60 are counted against principal centres only. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

UNFPA reported on 18 August 2025 that one commune, Masina in Kinshasa, [has a pilot at its municipal civil-status office](<https://drc.unfpa.org/fr/news/rdc-masina-commune-pilote-pour-la-digitalisation-des-faits-de-letat-civil>). The pilot [aims to automate the collection and management of data on births, marriages and deaths](<https://drc.unfpa.org/fr/news/rdc-masina-commune-pilote-pour-la-digitalisation-des-faits-de-letat-civil>). Terms of reference posted on 3 April 2026 state that [the civil registers are mostly manual](<https://www.mediacongo.net/dpics/filesmanager/jobaof/2026/04-avril/03/ug_260413_01_05.pdf>). In the last twelve months, a [UNDP tender closing on 25 April 2026 sought a consultant to assess the digitalisation of civil registration](<https://allbusiness.africa/tenders/undp-cod-ic-crvs-2604-05-strategic-innovation-2026>). No source has been found that says any birth or death has been registered digitally. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

On 22 September 2026 ACSI, the agency that built the system Congo calls SIFEC, [handed the system's operating documents to the territorial administration directorate](<https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/digitalisation-de-letat-civil-ladministration-du-territoire-receptionne-les-documents>). After the handover [seven steps remained, user training and deployment among them](<https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/digitalisation-de-letat-civil-ladministration-du-territoire-receptionne-les-documents>). In the last twelve months, on 20 February 2026 a workshop at Kintélé [validated 17 recommendations on SIFEC](<http://www.finances.gouv.cg/fr/articles/cloture-travaux-SIFEC_200226>). In 2021 the World Bank found [electronic records stored locally](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/801771619776798100/txt/Concept-Project-Information-Document-PID-Congo-Digital-Acceleration-Project-P175592.txt>) in some centres of Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire. No office has been found using SIFEC, and nothing since 2021 says whether those local records are still kept. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

The Ministry of the Interior's [strategic plan for modernising civil registration runs from 2024 to 2028](<http://comoresdroit.centerblog.net/2878-le-comite-de-pilotage-du-projet-amecc-ii>). Births, marriages and deaths [are registered in paper registers](<http://comoresdroit.centerblog.net/2912-une-revolution-numerique-se-prepare-pour-l-etat-civil>), and the digital system, an eCRVS, [is only proposed, by a preliminary study](<http://comoresdroit.centerblog.net/2912-une-revolution-numerique-se-prepare-pour-l-etat-civil>). In the last twelve months, the study was [launched in Moroni on 2 October 2025](<https://www.lagazettedescomores.com/soci%C3%A9t%C3%A9/vers-un-%C3%A9tat-civil-num%C3%A9rique-moh%C3%A9li-ouvre-la-voie-%C3%A0-la-modernisation-nationale-.html>) and [validated on 25 March 2026](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/comoros-advances-digital-identity-reform-with-nationwide-registry-overhaul>). On 11 March 2026 the Council of Ministers [did not adopt the draft decree for a national civil status agency](<https://beit-salam.km/actualit%C3%A9s/conseil-des-ministres-du-11-mars-2026-des-initiatives-pour-l%E2%80%99agriculture,-la-s%C3%A9curit%C3%A9,-l%E2%80%99innovation-et-l%E2%80%99environnement.html>). No source has been found that says when the pilot starts, or that any office keeps records other than on paper. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

UNICEF's profile, compiled to November 2017, states that [all vital events are recorded directly in the computer](<https://data.unicef.org/crvs/cabo-verde/>). It puts the applications in [the conservatórias of all 22 municipalities](<https://data.unicef.org/crvs/cabo-verde/>). Registration stations [exist only in the urban centres of those municipalities](<https://data.unicef.org/crvs/cabo-verde/>). The Civil Registry Code of 2014 [requires entries in electronic form, held in a national civil registry database](<https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/Download/1940>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share of offices newer than 2017 has been found. Nothing shows whether the entry made at the conservatória reaches the national register. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

The Ville de Djibouti stated on 28 April 2024 that [the registration of births, marriages, divorces and deaths in Djibouti-Ville has rested since 2011 on software](<https://villededjibouti.dj/actualite2.php?id=31>). Terms of reference of February 2024 list [nine civil-status sites, all in Djibouti-Ville](<https://expertise-france.gestmax.fr/_expertise_france/public_files/mdj-tdr-diagnostic-etat-civil-vf.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. A 2025 ESCWA survey, found only in summary, says local offices hold no electronic records of births or deaths. Nothing dated 2025 or 2026 says any office outside Djibouti-Ville enters digitally, and no national count of offices has been found. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

[Law 14-08 of 9 August 2014 creates the national automated civil-status register under the Ministry of the Interior and Local Authorities](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-FRANCAIS/2014/F2014049.pdf>). The ministry's deck of 19 June 2019 shows [1,541 commune databases where entry, control and update are done](<https://www.id4africa.com/2019_event/presentations/InF3/4-Abderrazak-Henni-MOI-Algeria.pdf>). Under the 2014 law [each commune still inscribes acts on three paper registers kept in duplicate](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-FRANCAIS/2014/F2014049.pdf>). In the last twelve months the register was cited and not changed. In July 2026 the ministry presented it as [its own, created in 2014](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-decentralisation-algeria.pdf>). No total of local offices has been found against the 1,541. No source says the entry is made at the commune office at registration. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

Egypt's presentation to the 2026 APAI-CRVS registrars-general meeting gives [full nationwide automation of 4,571 health offices across the 27 governorates](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-egypt_crvs_transformation_journey.pdf>). A conference paper on the system implemented in 2017 states that [data entry is done at the health office](<http://www.au.int/sites/default/files/newsevents/workingdocuments/37474-wd-crvs-v-the_electronic_birth_and_death_registration_system_in_egypt.pdf>). The planning ministry's report of 2 August 2025 says [4,666 health offices are electronically linked](<https://mped.gov.eg/singlenews?id=6465>). In the last twelve months, on 20 January 2026 the health ministry [instructed all health affairs directorates to unify and improve their data's quality](<https://www.newsroom.info/263435>). No total of health offices has been found against either count. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

Eritrea's five-year Strategic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics Plan for 2024-2028 is [recorded by the African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child in observations adopted in April 2026](<https://reporting.acerwc.africa/sites/default/files/2026-07/503.26_Eritrea%20Concluding%20Observations%2022.07.2026.pdf>). A Dutch foreign ministry report of February 2017 says births and deaths are [registered in the sub-zoba's digital database after entry in the kebabi's handwritten register](<https://fln.dk/media/ow3jujfq/erit402.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing has been found on how a birth is entered today. No count of offices doing the digital entry has been found. Operating would need a published share, or a count with its total, showing more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

In July 2026 Ethiopia's rollout of its national eCRVS [begins with a pilot in Addis Ababa](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-digitization-ethiopia.pdf>), then Amharic-speaking regions, then the rest of the country. A tablet system, ME-CRVS, [has been piloted in 1,300 kebeles and health facilities](<https://www.child-identity.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Taju-Mohammed-Presentation.pdf>). In January 2025 the city agency's digitisation was [in a pilot phase in 21 of 116 woredas](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202501/school-registration-adds-up-to-expanding-use-cases-of-ethiopias-digital-id>). In the last twelve months, the mayor of Addis Ababa launched the Integrated Civil Registration and Residency Service Technology on 5 December 2025. He [announced full implementation in 50 woredas from 8 December](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_7858122>). No source has been found that shows any digital system past its pilot outside Addis Ababa. None gives the rollout phase reached by July 2026. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

Law 008/2022 of 15 June 2022 makes the Centre National de l'Etat Civil (CNEC) [the public service that builds the digital, biometric and centralised civil register](<https://journal-officiel.ga/18873-008-2022-/>). The World Bank described the civil registry as [entirely paper-based](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/301741627956043619/pdf/Gabon-Digital-Gabon-Project.pdf>) in June 2021. In the last twelve months, on 28 September 2026 [an inter-ministerial workshop opened at Ntoum](<https://www.gabonreview.com/etat-civil-des-experts-reunis-a-ntoum-pour-preparer-la-reforme-numerique/>) to define the conditions for putting the CNEC into operation. [A mapping exercise to prioritise the departments whose offices will register digitally was under way at 31 May 2026](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099062726133542471/pdf/P175987-e83bc197-693c-4c5b-bf60-39949daa03f8.pdf>). No pilot office has been named, and the CNEC is not yet in operation. Establishing would need births entered digitally at registration, past any pilot, in some local offices.

The Births and Deaths Registry [develops and administers the births and deaths registration system under Act 1027 of 2020](<https://afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2026-09/Evidence%20Generation%20for%20Suicide%20Prevention%20in%20Ghana.%20A%20Situational%20Analysis.pdf>). Births in Ablekuma West, a municipal district of Greater Accra, are [registered on the Registry's digital registration platform](<https://getinthepicture.org/system/files/sites/default/files/C1_Session%204.2_Owusu_Paper_0.pdf>), which [registered 1,722 of them from March to October 2024](<https://getinthepicture.org/system/files/sites/default/files/C1_Session%204.2_Owusu_Paper_0.pdf>). In April 2025 the Acting Registrar said the Registry was [taking steps to digitise all offices](<https://gna.org.gh/2025/04/all-16-regions-to-receive-new-office-complexes-bdr-acting-registrar/>). In the last twelve months, in 2026, the Eastern Regional Registrar said [officers are expected to complete birth registrations digitally in communities](<https://www.modernghana.com/news/1530759/unicef-bdr-and-kuami-eugene-push-for-improved.html>). No national count or share of local offices entering births digitally has been found. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration, into the national register.

Guinea's 2023 civil status law [makes the ministry in charge of civil status responsible for the equipment of civil status centres](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/118843/GIN-118843.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the territorial administration ministry [launched the RENEC civil status register project through ONECI](<https://guistat.com/guinee-le-matd-lance-via-loneci-le-projet-renec-pour-moderniser-et-securiser-letat-civil/>). [RENEC is paid for from the national development budget](<https://guistat.com/guinee-le-matd-lance-via-loneci-le-projet-renec-pour-moderniser-et-securiser-letat-civil/>). On 2 September 2026 Ratoma commune's civil status officer said [commune offices establish digital birth certificates on secure paper](<https://mosaiqueguinee.com/2026/09/etat-civil-la-guinee-confrontee-a-une-penurie-dactes-de-naissance-numeriques/>). Printing had stopped for about two weeks because the paper had run out. No count or share of offices has been found, and no source says the entry is made at the office. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally when they are registered.

The Registrar General said that by June 2026 [over 1.4 million people were registered in the system he calls the eCRVS](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-interoperability-gambia.pdf>). [They were issued a birth certificate](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-interoperability-gambia.pdf>). A 2025 World Bank diagnostic counts [79 civil registration offices with digitalised registers issuing birth certificates in 2025](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102025103014657/pdf/P502279-e8627dee-4568-45e7-bb51-9a1aea1ff040.pdf>). In the last twelve months, a [Civil Registration and Vital Statistics Bill had its first reading in the National Assembly on 5 March 2026](<https://www.voicegambia.com/2026/03/06/civil-registration-bill-2026-receives-first-reading-in-national-assembly/>). The total number of civil registration offices has not been found, so the 79 have no share. No source states that the record is keyed at the registration point when the birth is registered. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration, shown by a share or a count with its total.

The system the country calls SIREC [was implemented at the Ministry of Justice's Direção-Geral de Identificação Civil, Registo e Notariado](<https://www.instituto-camoes.pt/sobre/comunicacao/noticias/guine-bissau-evento-de-encerramento-do-projeto-gestdoc-e-lancamento-dos-sistemas-passe-e-sirec>), launched in January 2025. In the last twelve months, in the first quarter of 2026, Santa Luzia [became the first civil registry office in the country to operate entirely digitally](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2026-04/_undp_g.b_newsletter_jan-mar_2026_eng_1.pdf>). In June 2026 a mobile caravan [was to take birth registration on SIREC to 16 communities](<https://ang.gw/pnud-e-uniao-europeia-lancam-terceira-edicao-da-candonga-di-justica-2026/>). The statistics office [counts 13 conservatórias and 80 registry posts](<https://www.stat-guinebissau.com/Menu_principal/IV_RGPH/rgph1/projecoes/Anuario%20Final_de_Estatisticas_Vitais.pdf>) in its yearbook for 2018 to 2022. The number of offices and posts entering records digitally, set against that total, has not been found. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally into the national register.

The Ministry of Justice [put the system it calls SIREC into service in December 2018](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/discurso_de_la_representante_de_unicef_en_el_dia_del_ni%C3%B1o_africano_2021>), with the support of UNICEF and the European Union. The World Bank said in 2024 that the pilot in Malabo [allows the digital registration of new births](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051724134540301/txt/P179339-f4a4c89e-b212-4802-9f00-4c68aefed3c8.txt>). It said the seven regional offices [collect and store data on paper](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051724134540301/txt/P179339-f4a4c89e-b212-4802-9f00-4c68aefed3c8.txt>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the state IT centre CNIAPGE told parliament that in 2025 it had [set up a new system to register newborns from hospitals](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/continuan_las_comparecencias_de_los_miembros_del_gobierno_en_la_comision_parlamentaria_que_analiza_los_presupuestos_generales>). How the pilot and the hospital system make the record has not been found. Nor has the number of offices using them. Establishing would need births entered digitally when they are registered, past the pilot, in some local offices.

Civil Registration Services [sits in the Ministry of Interior and National Administration's State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services](<https://www.knbs.or.ke/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/2023-Kenya-Vital-Statistics-Report.pdf>), under an executive order of January 2023. In the last twelve months, ESTDEV said in September 2026 that [more than 270,000 births were registered in two months](<https://www.estdev.ee/en/articles/over-270000-births-registered-two-months-kenyas-e-birth-registry-developed-together>) through the new digital birth registration solution. Parents [confirm the birth and enter the data while still in the hospital](<https://www.estdev.ee/en/articles/over-270000-births-registered-two-months-kenyas-e-birth-registry-developed-together>). The Star reported in March 2026 that the Civil Registration Service [led the validation of the Births and Deaths Registration Bill 2025](<https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/realtime/2026-03-05-government-moves-to-introduce-digital-civil-registration-system>). The number of hospitals or offices using the system has not been found. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally when they are registered.

The Ministry of Health [registers and certifies births and deaths through its Bureau of Vital Statistics](<https://moh.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/Ministry-of-Health-Annual-Report.pdf>), by its report for 2024. The report says [birth and death registration have been integrated into the DHIS2 platform](<https://moh.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/Ministry-of-Health-Annual-Report.pdf>). In May 2024 the World Bank found [most services at the 15 County Service Centers remained paper-based](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099052924164514688/pdf/BOSIB-0aa50b62-6e1c-4715-bcbb-a6d38f4bdc2e.pdf>). UNICEF Liberia in December 2024 counted birth registration services in [all 15 counties and 58 centres](<https://www.unicef.org/liberia/press-releases/new-era-inclusion-millions-children-gain-legal-identity>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says how many of the 58 centres enter births on the platform. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally, shown by a published share or a count given with its total.

The Civil Registration Authority [manages the collection of births and deaths data and issues the legal documents](<https://seha.ly/media/statistics_reports/vital-statistics-report-for-the-year-2020mD5xx9G.pdf>), the 2022 vital statistics report says. The report states that [all of the Authority's offices are fully automated and electronically linked to its centre](<https://seha.ly/media/statistics_reports/vital-statistics-report-for-the-year-2020mD5xx9G.pdf>). It counts [12 branches, 133 issuing offices and at least 380 service offices](<https://seha.ly/media/statistics_reports/vital-statistics-report-for-the-year-2020mD5xx9G.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 1 March 2026, the Attorney General's office reported that he had [discussed the project to create the electronic civil registry database with the head of the Authority](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=351962&lang=ar>). Whether a birth is entered at the office when it is registered has not been found. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

The Department of National Identity and Civil Registry, in the Ministry of Home Affairs, [is the lead agency for civil registration](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-interoperability-lesotho.pdf>), it said in July 2026. In the last twelve months, UNICEF Lesotho reported on 5 August 2026 that [30 birth registration stations had been established in health facilities](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/unicef-lesotho_foreverychild-digitaltransformation-activity-7490765967325597697-36h5>), in Maseru, Berea and Leribe. In July 2026 the Department listed [nationwide scale-up of digital birth registration as an action for 2026-2027](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-interoperability-lesotho.pdf>). A World Bank note of May 2022 says [all 15 enrolment centres that allow for birth registration are linked to a central server](<https://openknowledge.worldbank.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/9ba0954b-f540-5038-9311-d1bd69f69cf6/content>). No total of local registration offices is published. Neither count is a share. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration.

In October 2024 the Ministry of the Interior said its civil-status system SGEC [handles birth and death declarations digitally](<https://aujourdhui.ma/actualite/registre-national-linterieur-renforce-son-dispositif-digital-de-letat-civil>). It was [generalised to all the Kingdom's civil-status offices](<https://aujourdhui.ma/actualite/registre-national-linterieur-renforce-son-dispositif-digital-de-letat-civil>). In April 2025 its territorial authorities directorate was [running a project to digitise the registers and build one information system for 1,821 offices](<https://fr.le360.ma/politique/vaste-projet-de-numerisation-des-registres-de-letat-civil_2D3JKX433FBJ5JN747O5G2VFOU/>). In the last twelve months, the World Bank gave its civil registry back-office system as [operational in 59 of 97 participating municipalities on 30 June 2024](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099030926112020747/pdf/P168147-76ebb47f-2ef4-42ba-8d67-88b617eb1f27.pdf>). The figure was [unchanged on 30 January 2026](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099030926112020747/pdf/P168147-76ebb47f-2ef4-42ba-8d67-88b617eb1f27.pdf>). No count of offices registering digitally has been set against the country's total. Operating would need such a count to show more than half of local offices entering births digitally.

A decree of 2 December 2020 [set up the Centre National d'État Civil et de l'Identité under the technical supervision of the Interior ministry](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/114753/MDG-114753.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the World Bank reported that communes using the digital registration system SIECM [rose from 75 to 336 in the six months to December 2025](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099121925094025414/txt/P169413-92234883-0626-410f-a2c4-c2b2e93265f7.txt>). It gives the 336 as 40% of the project's target. In March 2026 the Unité de Gouvernance Digitale described the birth registration platform as [being deployed progressively at national scale](<https://digital.gov.mg/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/26-03-02-TDR-AUDIT-IDMS.pdf>). The share of all communes using the system has not been found. Nothing found says what has funded the system since the project's financing closed on 30 June 2026. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally.

An ordinance of 14 February 2025 [creates the Agence nationale de Sécurisation des Actes d'Etat civil, a national public establishment](<https://sgg-mali.ml/JO/2025/mali-jo-2025-05.pdf>). A platform approved by December 2024 [is to consolidate births, deaths and marriages](<https://www.unicef.org/mali/en/stories/celebration-progress-birth-registration-mali>). The National Directorate of Civil Status [had identified ten pilot areas for the platform](<https://www.unicef.org/mali/en/stories/celebration-progress-birth-registration-mali>). In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the head of digitalisation at the Directorate [described the birth chain as paper](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-decentralisation-mali_0.pdf>). It [named complete digitalisation of the system as a priority](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-decentralisation-mali_0.pdf>). No office has been found entering an event digitally. Whether the pilots have started has not been found. Establishing would need births entered digitally when they are registered, past any pilot, in some local offices.

The National Director of Registries and Notaries said in 2025 that [all 68 civil registration conservatories are digitised](<https://www.child-identity.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Arnaldo-ENglish-Reuniao-de-Lanc%C2%B8amento-Regional-do-Quadro-de-Programa-Estrate%C2%B4gico-para-o-Fortalecimento-do-RCEV-ENGL-1-002-en-GB.pdf>). The Directorate [holds the main database of the system it calls e-RCEV](<https://civil.registos.gov.mz/crvs/Home/About>). In the last twelve months, Jornal Notícias reported on 24 September 2026 that [the justice sector is installing 100 civil registration posts in health units with maternity wards](<https://jornalnoticias.co.mz/destaque/registo-civil-chega-a-mais-100-maternidades/>). About 250 birth registration posts already work, about 25 per cent of some 1,000 health units. The posts below the conservatories are left out of the digitised count. Nothing found shows whether the new maternity posts enter the record digitally. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally, shown by a share or a count with its total.

Law 2025-011 of 24 February 2025 [requires a birth to be declared within 60 clear days at the Centre d'Accueil des Citoyens](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/117696/MRT-117696.pdf>). Law 2011-003 [has births and deaths declared at the centre and recorded in the central database](<https://www.coursupreme.mr/docs/loi0032011.pdf>). The population register agency's director general said on 3 August 2021 that [153 citizen reception centres had been received and equipped](<https://www.ami.mr/archives/119459>). [There were to be 168, built in communes and administrative centres](<https://www.ami.mr/archives/119459>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Outside the law, nothing found says a centre enters a birth digitally when it is declared. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally at registration, shown by a share or a count with its total.

The Civil Status Division's report for 2023/2024 says [the CSD System has run since November 2001](<https://csd.govmu.org/DocumentsList/FINALISED%20ANNUAL%20REPORT%20CSD.pdf>). It counts [36 Civil Status Offices](<https://csd.govmu.org/DocumentsList/FINALISED%20ANNUAL%20REPORT%20CSD.pdf>) and gives no share entering records. On 2 September 2025 the Division announced that [its CSD System was being revamped](<https://csd.govmu.org/Documents/Communique/Communique%20-%20Revamping%20of%20CSD%20System%20New%20.pdf>). [Offices opened on 6 and 7 September 2025 to register births and deaths](<https://csd.govmu.org/Documents/Communique/Communique%20-%20Revamping%20of%20CSD%20System%20New%20.pdf>) during the revamp. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source from the last three years says births are entered at the office, or gives a share of offices doing so. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally, shown by a published share.

The National Registration Bureau, under the Ministry of Homeland Security, [is the body responsible for civil registration](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2026-01/malawi_nrb_strategic_plan_2025_web.pdf>), and its plan of September 2025 says [kits at district registration offices register births and deaths and print the certificates](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2026-01/malawi_nrb_strategic_plan_2025_web.pdf>). UNDP counts [87 service points in five districts in 2025](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2026-02/undp_idt4m_annual_report_2025_web.pdf>), against [415 Traditional and Sub-Traditional Authorities listed for expansion by 2030](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2026-02/undp_idt4m_annual_report_2025_web.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in July 2026, [74 health facilities issued instant birth certificates through Nzika](<https://www.undp.org/malawi/stories/securing-childrens-future-through-digital-birth-registration-malawi>), with no total given. On 9 October 2026 [UNDP handed over 152 printers](<https://malawi24.com/2026/10/09/printers-to-bring-registration-services-closer-to-malawians/>). No share of local offices registering digitally is published. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally.

[The Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security registers births and deaths on the National Population Registration System](<https://nsa.org.na/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/2018-2021_Namibia-Vital-Statistics-Report_April-2024.pdf>), the statistics agency said in April 2024. [The system's death module was deployed in 2012 and its birth module in 2013](<https://unstats.un.org/legal-identity-agenda/documents/Paper/2023/CRVSID-Namibia.pdf>). The agency also said that [some registration offices in remote areas lack computers or internet connectivity, which delays capture](<https://nsa.org.na/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/2018-2021_Namibia-Vital-Statistics-Report_April-2024.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [in December 2025 the ministry said it had deployed its staff to 24 state hospitals](<https://www.namibian.com.na/home-affairs-deploys-staff-to-24-hospitals-for-instant-birth-registration/>). They issue birth certificates right after delivery. No count or share of local offices registering digitally is published. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally, shown by a share or a count with its total.

[The computerised system was in production in 101 of 266 communes and communal arrondissements in December 2024](<https://stat-niger.org/wp-content/uploads/etat_civil/rapport_etat_civil_2023.pdf>), by the statistics office. [The government counted 102 communes on 22 April 2026](<https://www.gouv.ne/index.php/les-communiques-du-gouvernement/1143-conclusions-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-mercredi-22-avril-2026>). In the last twelve months, [an ordinance of 22 April 2026 provides for the national civil-status register](<https://www.gouv.ne/index.php/les-communiques-du-gouvernement/1143-conclusions-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-mercredi-22-avril-2026>), and [its decree followed on 18 May 2026](<https://www.gouv.ne/index.php/les-communiques-du-gouvernement/1171-conclusions-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-lundi-18-mai-2026>). On 11 August 2026 the ministry [announced the computerisation of all communes and declaration centres and a new platform as works to come](<https://anp.ne/lancement-a-tahoua-dune-tournee-nationale-de-vulgarisation-des-textes-juridiques-et-des-operations-denregistrement-intermediaire-au-registre-national-de-la-population/>). Whether village declaration centres are computerised is not stated. Operating would need more than half of local offices entering births digitally.

The National Population Commission says births and deaths [have been registered digitally across the country since 1 July 2026](<https://von.gov.ng/commission-commences-nationwide-digital-birth-death-registration/>). It calls the platform VitalReg. In the last twelve months, the platform [became operational in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory on 1 July 2026](<https://von.gov.ng/national-population-commission-launches-digital-registration-platform/>), replacing paper. On 18 July 2026 the Registrar General's Department reported [3,372 wards activated and 304 registration workstations deployed](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-digitisation-nigeria.pdf>). A registrar in Lagos said in August 2026 that his team [takes details on a form when the network fails](<https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/08/3-5m-missing-births-how-hospitals-can-close-nigerias-registration-gap/>). No total of wards has been found. The 4,011 registration centres are not said to enter on the platform. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

Rwanda's statistics institute states that in 2025 its civil registration system, NCI-CRVS, is [fully operational at all five categories of registration office](<https://statistics.gov.rw/sites/default/files/documents/2026-04/Rwanda%20Civil%20Registration%20Vital%20Statistics%202025_0.pdf>). They are health facilities, cells, sectors, districts and embassies. The finance law of 30 June 2026 [appropriates RWF 116,184,997 to civil registration for 2026/27, domestically financed](<https://www.minecofin.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/Minecofin/Publications/REPORTS/National_Budget/Annual_State_Finance_Laws/2026_to_2027_Original_Annual_Finance_Law/2026-2027_Original_Annual_Finance_Law.pdf>). In the last twelve months, birth registration completeness [rose from 90.3% in 2024 to 92.9% in 2025](<https://statistics.gov.rw/sites/default/files/documents/2026-04/Rwanda%20Civil%20Registration%20Vital%20Statistics%202025_0.pdf>), and death registration completeness rose from 46.1% to 50.5%. The share of deaths registered within 30 days fell from 96.3% to 89.9%. No count of offices using the system and no rural share has been found. Mature would need at least 90 per cent of local offices registering births and deaths digitally, on a figure published within two years that gives the rural share.

The civil registry centre of South Gezira locality [issued an electronic birth certificate at its Al-Hosh office on 17 May 2026](<https://alnawrs.com/212689>). Landinfo reported in March 2023 a [centralised electronic registry introduced in 2011](<https://landinfo.no/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Report-Sudan-Civil-Registration-ID-documents-and-passports-03032023.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the Al-Hosh office [resumed work in May 2026 after a stoppage caused by insecurity and displacement](<https://alnawrs.com/212689>). The governor of Gezira State [inaugurated civil registry work in Umm al-Qura locality on 29 April 2026](<https://alnawrs.com/209412>). A lawyer told the BBC in August 2026 that the conflict in Darfur [has shut down civil registry offices](<https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cr7kldz4djno>). Nothing since the war began says how a birth record is made. No total of offices has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

On the data of the civil status agency, ANEC, its system held [14,839,577 births and 487,259 deaths at 17 July 2026](<https://lesoleil.sn/actualites/societe-fait-divers/etat-civil-lanec-franchit-le-cap-des-70-de-deploiement-du-lgec/>). Its software, the LGEC, was in [437 of the 629 centres, 70%](<https://lesoleil.sn/actualites/societe-fait-divers/etat-civil-lanec-franchit-le-cap-des-70-de-deploiement-du-lgec/>). In the last twelve months, ANEC's director general said on 5 August 2026 that the [LGEC had passed its pilot phase](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Dossier/enquete-nes-mais-invisibles-33-un-enfant-sur-cinq-nest-toujours-pas-enregistre-a-letat-civil-au-senegal-les-eclairages-du-dg-de-lanec_n_500404.html>). By 16 September 2026 [deployment was effective in the Dakar, Thiès, Louga, Diourbel, Fatick and Kaolack regions](<https://aps.sn/etat-civil-77-des-centres-couverts-par-le-processus-de-modernisation-dg-anec/>). He put the modernisation process at 77% of the 629 centres. Every figure counts centres digitised, deployed or covered. None counts centres entering events in the system, and no rural share has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

In May 2024 the National Civil Registration Authority (NCRA) [presented the integrated eCRVS and ID management system as its own](<https://id4africa.com/2024/ps2/PS2-3-Sierra-Leone-Final.pdf>). NCRA told the ID4Africa meeting of 22 May 2025 that [over 80% of its services are digitised](<https://www.id4africa.com/2025/files/T2-P1-S2-4-SIERRALEONE_FINAL.pdf>), birth and death registration among them. In March 2023 UNICEF reported that [at NCRA's hospital centres the child's details are entered when the mother registers the birth](<https://www.unicef.org/sierraleone/stories/making-birth-registration-more-accessible-every-child-sierra-leone>). In the last twelve months, UNICEF said in October 2026 that [digital birth registration is now part of the civil registration system](<https://www.unicef.org/digitalimpact/stories/putting-children-heart-sierra-leones-digital-public-infrastructure>). No count or share of offices entering events digitally has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

Somalia's Law No. 46, [published on 5 April 2026](<https://www.osagsomalia.com/media/documents/bulletins-contents/legislation/2026/sharciga_Dad-dhigista_iyo_Tirakoobka_Xaaladaha_Madaniga.pdf>), charges a Directorate under the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation with creating and running a digital registration system. In the last twelve months, OpenCRVS's country page of January 2026 [counts 30 districts](<https://www.opencrvs.org/about-us/country-stories/somalia>). The ministry had [launched a pilot of the Unified Digital Civil Registration Service in 19 districts on 10 August 2025](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/1108-48024-somalia-pilots-19-district-digital-civil-registry-lays-groundwork-for-nationwide-legal-identity>). OpenCRVS counts 28,391 completed birth registrations. No total of districts or offices has been found, so no share can be read, and reports of the number of districts differ. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

The World Bank's [diagnostic of May 2026](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099053126171570627/pdf/P502463-0c06abde-be3d-4f83-b9e1-eca068e7bc1e.pdf>) gives the Directorate of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passports and Immigration as operator and owner of the planned civil registration system. It found that [birth registration is yet to be implemented and birth certificates do not exist](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099053126171570627/pdf/P502463-0c06abde-be3d-4f83-b9e1-eca068e7bc1e.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 24 July 2026 the government [announced plans for a digital system recording births, deaths, marriages and divorces](<https://www.eyeradio.org/government-to-adopt-modern-digital-birth-death-and-marriage-records-system/>). On 31 July 2026 the Directorate was reported to be [planning to link civil registration with the national ID system](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202607/south-sudan-plans-interoperable-birth-registration-digital-id-systems>). No office registering digitally has been described, and no design, procurement, pilot office or start date has been found. Establishing would need births entered digitally, past any pilot, in some local offices.

The chief conservator of the civil registry said in March 2026 that [births are registered by entering the data directly into the directorate's database](<https://rstp.st/2026/03/10/direcao-geral-dos-registos-e-notariados-com-mais-de-3-mil-registos-de-nascimento-por-ano/>). The World Bank said in 2023 that its system, SIGA, was [implemented by 2018 and registers births, deaths and marriages](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099032824212523838/pdf/P171592-effa7cbb-e47a-4467-bd3c-4bf28f84f93f.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the chief conservator said the directorate [is eliminating paper by registering births directly from the maternities](<https://rstp.st/2026/03/10/direcao-geral-dos-registos-e-notariados-com-mais-de-3-mil-registos-de-nascimento-por-ano/>). The chief conservator said registration is done in all the country's maternities. In 2023 the World Bank counted [11 centres and seven birth registration posts in maternities](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099032824212523838/pdf/P171592-effa7cbb-e47a-4467-bd3c-4bf28f84f93f.pdf>). No share of local offices entering records has been published. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

The Central Statistical Office's report for 2022 says births and deaths [are captured into the National Population Register on registration](<https://www.afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2023-10/Vital%20Statistics%20Report%202022%20%281%29.pdf>). It also says [the registration officer fills the form by hand and a typist enters it into the register](<https://www.afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2023-10/Vital%20Statistics%20Report%202022%20%281%29.pdf>). The Ministry of Home Affairs' 2024/25 report gives [15 service centres and 5 hospital registration points](<https://parliament.gov.sz/publications/parliament_reports/docs/ANNUAL%20REPORT%20HOME%20AFFAIRS.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the World Bank appraised the Digital Eswatini Project on 8 June 2026 [to upgrade the existing ID and civil registration systems](<https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099061826123027004/pdf/BOSIB-eeab9c88-27f5-404b-bf04-d448d9780618.pdf>). Its document says paper birth and death records are stored locally without centralised backups. No total of local offices has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

The Civil Status Act, [as in force on 1 November 2022](<https://seylii.org/akn/sc/act/1883/4/eng@2022-11-01>), makes the Chief Officer of Civil Status keeper of the registers of births and deaths. It provides a Central Civil Status Office in Victoria and offices at Praslin, La Digue and Anse Royale. A contributed article in Seychelles Nation of 10 August 2018 states that [the Civil Status records were computerised in 1989](<https://www.nation.sc/article.html?id=259946>), with a computerised record kept beside the manual register. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says where the computerised record is entered, or how many local offices enter it. Establishing would need births entered digitally, past any pilot, in some local offices.

The World Bank states [Chad created ANATS in 2016](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099061124175525537/pdf/BOSIB1811b26290ef1a3561032ec244ac8a.pdf>), the institution in charge of operationalising the civil registry. An account published in June 2025 quotes ANATS's coordinator that [more than 120,000 children had been registered through hospital-based registry offices](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202506/chad-mali-senegal-pursue-birth-registration-reforms-to-close-gaps>) since 2023. It gives 97 digitised hospital points, to be raised to 600. In the last twelve months, on 23 September 2026 the commune of N'Djamena [launched a project to digitise its civil registry and signed a memorandum with ANATS](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/chad-n-djamena-launches-civil-registry-digitization-drive>). The town hall cited [the still heavy recourse to physical procedures](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/tchad-n-djamena-lance-la-numerisation-de-son-etat-civil>). No total of local offices has been found. Entry at the office is said only of six hospitals in 2023. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

In 2024 UNDP Togo [supported the development, deployment and operation of a digital birth registration platform](<https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/2025-07/rapport_annuel_2024_pnud_togo_soft_02.pdf>), piloted at one town hall, Golfe 3. In the last twelve months, on 21 August 2026 the territorial administration ministry [launched the re-reading of the 2009 civil status law](<https://levisionnaire.tg/etat-civil-au-togo-le-matglac-renforce-les-capacites-des-acteurs-pour-une-reforme-du-cadre-juridique/>). In November 2026 [e-Vital Togo began as a pilot in four communes](<https://togoscoop.tg/togo-e-vita-un-projet-pour-moderniser-lenregistrement-des-naissances-et-des-deces/>), financed by Vital Strategies. The digital ministry [tendered a sixteen-commune digitalisation pilot in July 2026, with German financing](<https://bk.numerique.gouv.tg/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/MESPTN-Consultant-international-2.pdf>). No source says how the record is made on the 2024 platform, or whether the 16 Savanes communes register on it. Establishing would need births entered digitally, past any pilot, in some local offices.

Tunisia's national civil status system, Madania, [holds births and deaths as well as marriages and divorces in a centralised database](<https://www.ids.ac.uk/publications/biometric-digital-id-in-africa/>), a 2025 report says. A 2020 account says the registrar [writes each event by hand in the paper register and then records it directly in the central database](<https://web.archive.org/web/20210124181106/https://crvssystems.ca/sites/default/files/assets/files/SocialProtection_5_Tunisia_e_WEB.pdf>). An IDRC chapter of 2020 counts 350 principal offices and 170 subsidiary offices. In the last twelve months, on 4 and 11 December 2025 [workshops trained civil status officers from 72 municipalities on the system](<https://tunisia.unfpa.org/fr/news/%C3%A9tat-civil-72-municipalit%C3%A9s-tunisiennes-sunissent-pour-une-meilleure-gestion-des-donn%C3%A9es>). No source gives the share of offices that enter events in Madania. Nothing on offices is dated after 2020. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

Tanzania's Registration Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency (RITA) [introduced the Civil Registration System in 2017 and runs it](<https://www.nao.go.tz/uploads/Performance_Audit_Report_on_the_Identification__Registration_and_Issuance_of_Birth_and_Death_Certificates.pdf>). The national audit of October 2024 found that at under-five registration centres officers record a birth by hand in a register and then enter it online by phone. RITA's monitoring plan counts [6,341 of 11,053 under-five registration centres as active](<https://www.nao.go.tz/uploads/Performance_Audit_Report_on_the_Identification__Registration_and_Issuance_of_Birth_and_Death_Certificates.pdf>), 57 per cent. In the last twelve months, Zanzibar's registration agency reported [a 2025/2026 improvement of its system, with streamlined workflows and a unified mobile app](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-decentralisation-tanzania_0.pdf>). No mainland change has been found in that time. The 57 per cent counts centres RITA calls active, not centres entering digitally. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

Uganda's National Identification and Registration Authority (NIRA) [holds all of Uganda's civil registration systems](<https://apai-crvs.uneca.org/sites/default/files/resourceuploads/day-2-interoperability-uganda.pdf>), it said on 18 July 2026. Its Mobile Vital Records System [registered 498,439 live births and 22,182 deaths in 2024](<https://www.ubos.org/wp-content/uploads/publications/Uganda-Vital-Statistics-Report-2024.pdf>), on the statistics bureau's figures. A 2020 brief says the system was [used in at least 112 of 135 districts](<https://crvssystems.ca/sites/default/files/assets/images/CRVS_Webinar_Uganda_e_WEB.pdf>). In the last twelve months, NIRA [registered 123,526 births and 9,935 deaths](<https://budget.finance.go.ug/sites/default/files/Sector%20Spending%20Agency%20Budgets%20and%20Performance/National%20Identification%20and%20Registration%20Authority_17.pdf>) in 2025/26 to 31 December 2025. On 18 July 2026 it said it had built a births and deaths module on its identity system. No share or count of offices making the entry has been found, and nothing on offices is dated after 2020. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

The Department of Home Affairs reports that [its online birth registration system was available at 242 health facilities by the end of 2024/25](<https://www.dha.gov.za/images/AnnualReports/DHA-Annual-Report-2024-25.pdf>). The National Department of Health counts [299 health facilities able to register births at the end of 2024/25](<https://www.health.gov.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/NDoH-2024-25-Annual-Report-_-19-September-2025.pdf>). The Annual Performance Plan 2026/27 also counts [325 front offices and 220 mobile offices](<https://pmg.org.za/files/2/DHA_APP_2026-27_Final_26_Mar_2026.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the Portfolio Committee on Home Affairs reports that [the 2025/26 target of automated birth registration at 47 health facilities was missed](<https://pmg.org.za/tabled-committee-report/6581/>). The rollout was deferred to 2026/27. No share of local offices registering births digitally has been found, and how the front offices make the record is not described. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

In a 2026 statement to the National Assembly the Minister of Home Affairs and Internal Security [describes INRIS as the ministry's civil registration system](<https://www.parliament.gov.zm/sites/default/files/images/publication_docs/INRIS%20IMPLEMENTATION%20-%20Mr%20Mwiimbu.pdf>), deployed in eleven districts. The ministry said in December 2025 that [about 1.3 million citizens have been enrolled on INRIS](<https://znbc.co.zm/?p=10211>). A September 2025 preprint states [death notification forms on paper are carried weekly from local offices to headquarters](<https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.09.09.25335397v1>) and entered there. In the last twelve months, the Lavushimanda district office [registered over 3,000 children under five in the four months to September 2026](<https://www.lusakatimes.com/2026/09/03/govt-implements-digital-civil-registration/>). In October 2023 [INRIS was rolled out in 79 districts](<https://dailynationzambia.com/2023/10/govt-digitises-nrcs/>). No count of offices that enter events in INRIS themselves has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.

The Deputy Registrar General said on 22 July 2026 that [all 10 provinces and 63 districts have been computerised](<https://www.zbcnews.co.zw/african-registrars-look-to-replicate-zimbabwes-e-passport-success/>), as have more than 20 of 209 sub-offices. UNICEF Zimbabwe stated in July 2025 that [computerised offices and sub-offices allow real-time data entry at the office](<https://www.unicef.org/zimbabwe/stories/zimbabwe-expands-civil-registration-services-hard-reach-areas>). In the last twelve months, in October 2025 the Minister of Home Affairs [announced plans to computerise sub-offices across the country](<https://www.heraldonline.co.zw/civil-registry-department-to-computerise-sub-offices/>). On 7 August 2026 UNICEF and the government [announced a China-funded project for 10 sub-offices in eight districts](<https://newziana.co.zw/unicef-government-move-to-digitise-birth-registration-services/>). UNICEF said some decentralised sub-offices are not computerised. No count of offices registering births digitally has been found. Operating would need a published share of local offices entering births digitally, or a count given with its total.
